title: Russian missile strike destroys apartment block in Dnipro
body:
On 14 January 2023 a Russian missile struck a nine-storey apartment building in Dnipro, a city on the Dnieper River in central-eastern Ukraine. The strike was part of a wider series of Russian missile attacks on Ukrainian cities that followed the full-scale invasion launched on 24 February 2022.

According to Ukrinform, which cited Ihor Klymenko, head of Ukraine's National Police, 36 civilians had been confirmed killed by 10:30 a.m. on 16 January, including two children. The same report said 75 people were injured, among them 15 children, and that 39 people had been rescued from the building, including six children.

Ukrinform reported that two sections of the building were destroyed from the second floor to the ninth floor. Seventy-two apartments were destroyed and more than 230 were damaged. Search and rescue teams and workers dismantling the rubble remained at the site while the figures were being reported, so the casualty count was still changing.

The Dnipro strike occurred during a period of Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure and residential areas in Ukraine in winter 2022-2023. Russian authorities have said they target military and energy-related sites, while Ukrainian officials have described such attacks on residential buildings as deliberate violence against civilians.
